The vulnerability has a layered causal chain: (1) commit 31c617c introduced ESInboundAdapter.updatePolicy() with a silent guard-on-nil-client return, establishing the pattern where policy updates require an active ES client. In the old daemon architecture this worked because policy was pushed over XPC after the filter started. (2) Commit 5a88795 merged daemon and filter into one process, placing applyPolicyToFilter() in XPCServer.init before adapter.start(), making the nil-client guard deterministically skip policy loading at startup and omitting a post-start cache clear. (3) Commit 614a794 refactored the init to main.swift but preserved the same ordering. Commit ddfdacb added the missing post-start cache clear; commit 56d617b then moved the full policy, allowlist, and jail-rule application after adapter startup. Local full-history ancestry, exact diffs, explicit Claude trailers, the upstream GitHub advisory, and both upstream fix patches were independently rechecked on 2026-07-31.

The vulnerability is a startup initialization ordering bug. Commit 5a88795 merged the daemon into opfilter as a single process, creating XPCServer which calls applyPolicyToFilter() in its init. This calls ESInboundAdapter.updatePolicy() which has 'guard let client else { return }' -- the ES client is nil because adapter.start() hasn't been called yet. Result: interactor.updatePolicy(rules) is never reached, so FilterInteractor retains only faaPolicy (baseline compile-time rules). Managed rules, user rules, and jail rules are silently dropped. Mute paths are correctly configured (adapter.start passes mergedRules to applyMutedPrefixes), so the kernel delivers events for the right paths, but enforcement decisions use incomplete rules. Commit 614a794 later moved the apply calls from XPCServer.init to main.swift but preserved the same before-start ordering. The fix (56d617b) moved applyPolicyToFilter/applyAllowlistToFilter/applyJailRulesToFilter to after adapter.start(), ensuring the ES client exists when they fire. All three origin commits have explicit Co-Authored-By trailers for Claude (Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6).

evidence.mechanism: The AI commit replaced Nashorn's --no-java evaluator with GraalJS HostAccess.ALL. The final fix disables host-class lookup, native access, threads, and process creation, directly reversing the new evaluator escape surface.

The AI commit exposed token-authenticated v1/v2 Users API resources by inheriting the base controller, while StoreUserRequest accepted any role and only checked authentication. The fix allowlists Admin/User and requires an existing Admin to assign Admin.

The AI member added /music/temp/ serving from a configurable temp directory and reused a separator-free startswith containment check. The fix appends the path separator; an older music path had the same flaw, so this is only the new temp-path contribution.

The AI-attributed revert removed the Azure certificate host allowlist, private-IP client, response-size cap, and generic error handling. The security fix restores those same controls, closing the SSRF and reachability oracle introduced by the revert.

The AI member retired the HTTPTrigger admission webhook while claiming CEL covered field rules, but RelativeURL and Prefix had no CEL validation. The final fix restores both CEL and Go validation for direct Kubernetes API creation.

accepted_edges.ai_signal: Generated with Claude Code; Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

evidence.mechanism: The AI member added Untar symlink extraction using archive-controlled entry names and link targets without destination containment. The fix validates both entry paths and symlink targets; older regular-file ZipSlip paths remain a separate pre-existing root.

The AI member resolved reply recipients by mutable username/nickname through user_list and used that result for delivery. The fix gates name matching behind an explicit dangerous opt-in and defaults to the stable webhook numeric user_id.

The AI member began fetching Matrix thread-root bodies into new session context without checking the root sender. The fix records sender IDs and drops thread/reply context that does not satisfy the room sender allowlist.

The AI member removed richer plugin, hook, and remote-gateway protections and simplified the model-facing config mutation guard to an incomplete set-diff/denylist. The fix expands protected settings and catches per-agent array edits. Two advisory records describe the same candidate/fix guard component and are counted once.

The AI member added exec-event delivery through heartbeat-runner, creating a system-triggered context that inherited senderIsOwner semantics. The fix adds ForceSenderIsOwnerFalse for exec completions and makes command authorization honor it.

The AI member introduced the Synology Chat channel with inherited default webhook paths and replaceExisting route registration, allowing multi-account route ownership collapse. The fix requires explicit unique paths and removes replacement behavior.

The AI member extended oauth-proxy passthrough to generic OAuth callbacks that consume parseGenericState without binding cookie state to the incoming nonce. The fix stores and compares oauthState for every caller, including oauth-proxy. The advisory has no CVE.

The AI member introduced content-hash deduplication by truncating SHA-256 to 16 hex characters and using that value as observation identity. The fix replaces the weak truncated hash used by computeObservationContentHash.

The Claude-authored CLI commit created --format csv and a hand-written escapeCsv that only handled RFC 4180 quoting. The fix prefixes nonnumeric cells beginning with formula triggers before CSV escaping.

The AI member added OUROBOROS_CLI_PATH as an execution-affecting environment override. Because project-local .env files were loaded, a cloned repository could point it at attacker code. The fix blocks CLI-path and backend selectors from project-local .env loading.
